thread.title: Apple Unveils iPhone XS, New Smartwatches At Product Launch Event | Investor's Business Daily

author: PATRICK SEITZ
title: Apple Unveils iPhone XS, New Smartwatches At Product Launch Event | Investor's Business Daily
text:
Consumer electronics giant Apple ( AAPL ) unveiled its 12th-generation smartphone, the iPhone XS, and its fourth-generation smartwatch, the Apple Watch Series 4, at a fall product launch event Wednesday.
X Pronounced "ten-ess," the iPhone XS is an updated version of the current 5.8-inch OLED-screen iPhone X. The X is the Roman numeral for 10. Apple also introduced a 6.5-inch OLED-screen model called the iPhone XS Max.
Both models have Face ID technology for secure log in using facial recognition. They also sport faster processors and better cameras than last year's iPhone X and iPhone 8 series.
"This is by far the most advanced iPhone we have ever created," Apple Chief Executive Tim Cook said at the event, held at the company's headquarters in Cupertino, Calif.
Promises 'New Era In Photography' Phil Schiller, senior vice president of worldwide marketing at Apple, touted the improved photography possible with the iPhone XS.
"You are going to be blown away with the pictures you will be able to take with the iPhone XS camera," he said.
The phone's dual-camera systems use enhanced sensors, processors and software to produce better photos. For instance, users will be able to change the depth of field on photos after they're snapped.
"This is a new era in photography," Schiller said. "Some people are calling it computational photography."
The iPhone XS also offers similar improvements for videography, he said.
In addition to the XS, Apple introduced a new 6.1-inch LCD-screen smartphone called the iPhone XR, which features an array of colorful case finishes. The device name is pronounced "ten-are."
Like the iPhone XS series, it uses Face ID for secure log-in and has improved cameras and processors.
Pricing, Availability For New iPhones The iPhone XS starts at $999 and the XS Max starts at $1,099. Both will be available for preorder starting Friday and will ship beginning on Sept. 21.
The iPhone XR starts at $749 and will be available for preorder starting on Oct. 19. It will start shipping on Oct. 26. That midrange handset comes in six colors: white, black, red, blue, yellow and coral.
Apple will keep two older models in its handset lineup at lower prices. The iPhone 7 now starts at $449 and the iPhone 8 starts at $599.
Apple Watch Series 4 Debuts Apple kicked off the product launch event by introducing the Apple Watch Series 4 .
"Apple Watch is not only the No. 1 smartwatch in the world, it's the No. 1 watch. Period," Cook said. "Apple Watch is redefining what a watch can do for you."
The Apple Watch Series 4 features larger displays and enhanced health features, such as heart-rate detection. The two new Apple Watch sizes have displays that are 32% and 35% larger than the previous models. The speaker has been redesigned and is 50% louder, so Siri responses are easier to hear. Plus the watches have improved sensors for more accurate activity tracking.
The new watches can detect low and fast heart rates and unusual rhythms, which could be atrial fibrillation. They also can now take electrocardiograms, an industry first for a smartwatch. Apple has received clearance from the Food and Drug Administration to promote the new health features, Apple Chief Operating Officer Jeff Williams said.
"Apple Watch has become an intelligent guardian for your health," Williams said.
The new smartwatches will be available beginning Sept. 21, starting at $399. Apple also lowered the prices for its Apple Watch Series 3, which it will keep in the lineup, starting at $279.
Fitbit ( FIT ) shares tumbled 6.7%, near 5.55, in afternoon trading Wednesday. Fitbit competes with Apple with wrist-worn activity trackers and its own fitness smartwatch.
No New AirPods Or AirPower The pre-holiday season product launch event ended without several rumored products. Many analysts expected Apple to introduce second-generation AirPods wireless earbuds and new iPad tablets.
The company's long-delayed AirPower wireless charging pad also was a no-show. Apple previewed the accessory at its fall product event last year, but said it wouldn't be released until sometime in 2018. The pad has room to wirelessly charge an iPhone X, Apple Watch and AirPods simultaneously.
To close the show, Cook announced improvements to the company's HomePod smart speaker. It added new features that let people do more with the Siri voice assistant on the wireless speaker. HomePod owners will be able to make and receive phone calls, set multiple timers, and search for music by song lyrics.
For instance, you can ask Siri to "play the song that goes 'I'm a rebel just for kicks now.' " That's if you can't remember the name of the song "Feel It Still" by Portugal. The Man. Of course, you can still ask Siri to play a particular song, artist or genre.
Apple stock fell 1.2% to close at 221.07 on the stock market today .
